item.title: Lions vs. Dolphins odds: Opening lines for Week 9 matchup
item.description: Aug 16, 2025; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions wide receiver Isaac TeSlaa (18) scores a touchdown against the Miami Dolphins in the second quarter at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Eamon Horwedel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions (5-2) will travel to Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins (1-6) in Week 9, in a battle between teams at two very different stages of their roster development. While the Lions are shaking off some early-season mistakes, they’ve strung together three wins, including back-to-back wins in their division, while the Dolphins are in the early stages of a rebuild under their latest regime. The folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -7 points . The Dolphins made a general manager and head coaching change this offseason, firing GM Chris Grier and coach Mike McDaniel after four unsuccessful seasons and hiring Jon-Eric Sullivan as their new GM and former Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley as their new coach. Like most new regimes, the new staff got to work early, cutting veteran contracts, including quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, wide receiver Tyreek Hill, and edge rusher Bradley Chubb. They also traded away former first-round pick Jaylen Waddle for a trio of picks to use in the 2026 NFL Draft to help them with the rebuild. Step one in establishing a new foundation was signing Malik Willis as their new signal caller—who most recently played in Green Bay with Hafley—and drafting six (!) rookie starters, including first-round picks guard Kadyn Proctor and corner Chris Johnson, as well as second-round pick linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, third-round receivers Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas, and fifth-round safety Michael Taaffe. They also have another eight rookies on their 53-man roster, meaning over 25% of the Dolphins roster (14 players) is made up of first-year players. As you would expect with a young roster at the beginning of a rebuild, the Dolphins have struggled out of the gate. In Week 1, the Raiders beat them by two touchdowns; the 49ers won by three touchdowns the week after; and the Chiefs beat them by two touchdowns in Week 3. In Week 4, they showed signs of improvement, losing to the Vikings by only five points; the Bengals won by just seven in Week 5, and in Week 6, they got their first win of the season, beating the Jets by three points. On Sunday, the Dolphins and Patriots squared off in an AFC East showdown, and while the Dolphins built a 13-3 lead at the half, the Patriots scored 21 unanswered points to go up 24-13 late in the fourth quarter. Willis connected on an explosive touchdown pass at the 2-minute warning to bring them close, but a failed 2-point conversion and a failed onside kick set the final score at 24-19. The Lions and Dolphins are scheduled to play on Sunday, November 8 at 1 p.m. ET at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida. Lions fans, download the SB Nation app today! item.title: Sunderland make Regis Le Bris decision with club rock-bottom of Premier League
item.description: Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris is set to remain in post despite a dismal start to the season, with the club rock-bottom of the Premier League after just one win from nine matches. PA reported on Monday that the Frenchman retains the full support of the club’s board and remains central to their plans, having come under increasing pressure during that dire run. Saturday’s 3-1 defeat at Coventry extended Sunderland’s winless league run to seven games, while they have collected just one point from five on the road. The club’s hierarchy recognise fans’ frustrations and share their disappointment with some below-par performances, but believe Le Bris can turn their fortunes around. The former Lorient head coach’s stock could not have been much higher in the summer. After leading the club to promotion via the play-offs, he guided them to an impressive seventh-placed finish in their first season back in the top flight after an eight-year absence, delivering European football for the first time in 53 years. While their domestic form has been dispiriting the Black Cats have made an unbeaten start to their Europa League campaign, with wins against AZ Alkmaar and Torreense and more recently a draw in Poland against Lech Poznan. The added fixtures appear to have taken a toll on the players’ top-flight performances, but Sunderland’s hierarchy feel their ambitions are best served by maintaining stability and adopting a collective responsibility. The Black Cats are next in action on Thursday against Europa League opponents Dinamo Zagreb at home before they face Chelsea at the Stadium of Light in the Premier League on Sunday. PA

item.description: LINCOLN, NEBRASKA - OCTOBER 31: Head coach Matt Rhule of the Nebraska Cornhuskers reacts to a call during the game against the Washington Huskies during the first half at Memorial Stadium on October 31, 2026 in Lincoln, Nebraska. item.title: Monday Dots: Offense Saves Tricks for Late, Snatches Treat of a Win
item.description: Happy Monday Dawg fans, and welcome to today’s Dots. Saturday’s win at Nebraska will be remembered as one of the most remarkable of Jedd Fisch’s tenure, as the Huskies pulled out a near-impossible win inside the last two minutes against the Cornhuskers, 17-10. Jedd got to have his QB cake and eat it too on Saturday, and his smile after the game said it all: Elijah Brown got the start, placating 95% of the Husky fanbase, while Demond Williams, Jr was unleashed in the 4th quarter to perform his high-wire magic act and deliver a conference victory on the road, at night, against a Husker team that recently had both Indiana and Oregon on the ropes. Demond’s insertion in the 4th quarter was indeed the “spark” Jedd said the team needed — and diverging stories would be written in re Demond’s play, depending on whether the arrow pointed to a “W” or an “L” at 00:00. A non-existent ground game (Brian Bonner, Trey Cooley, and Jayden Limar(!) carried 11 times for just 29 yards), and a short passing game from Brown meant that punter Hunter Green saw a lot of action… and let’s take a moment to recognize how great Green was: 8 punts, 48.9 yd avg., 5 kicks inside the 20, and a long of 63 yds. Sure, no team wants to punt 8 times, but Hunter Green was as important to this win as was Chris Lawson, IMO. And Lawson was magnificent himself: 12 catches, 155 yds, and the offense’s only TD on the night, putting UW ahead for good with 1:30 left in the game. Not to mention the falling, sideline catch on 4th-and-18 that set up his sensational touchdown. The Husky defense thwarted runs between the tackles, held all rushers to a 4.6 yd average, and allowed just one TD and one FG. Cornhusker dual-threat QB Anthony Colandrea ran for only 20 yds on 7 carries, wasn’t especially accurate, and looked nervous and indecisive throughout the game. He was picked off three times by Husky DBs, with Alex McLaughlin’s pick-six proving the winning margin. Now we have a familiar question but under very different circumstances: Which QB starts against Penn State this Saturday at Husky Stadium? item.title: Dodgers notes: Bob Wolfe retires, Ross Newhan dies, MLB lockout
item.description: Hollywood, - August 13: Los Angeles Dodgers, Chief Operating Officer Bob Wolfe looks on as Los Angeles Dodgers great, Orel Hershiser was honored with a star along the Hollywood Walk of Fame in Hollywood on Thursday, August 13, 2026. (Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images Dodgers executive vice president and chief operating officer Bob Wolfe will retire at the end of 2026, the club announced on Friday. He will shift into an advisory role. Wolfe has been with the Dodgers since Guggenheim Partners took over ownership of the team in 2012, and headed the club’s day-to-day business operations for the last 14-plus seasons. The longtime executive has worked with current Dodgers president and CEO Stan Kasten at multiple stops, beginning with the Atlanta Braves in 1980, plus the Atlanta Hawks and Washington Nationals before coming with Kasten to Los Angeles. Wolfe worked with Kasten for the first 12 of the Braves’ first 12 of 14 division titles in a row and for the last 14 Dodgers postseason berths. “Having worked 47 years in team sports, I’ve been more entertained than anyone deserves,” Wolfe said in a statement. “It’s been a privilege to ride the coattails of so many on- and off-the-field Hall of Famers, will-be Hall of Famers and should-be Hall of Famers. With Stan always providing the vision, I’ve had the latitude to work closely with the talented individuals and departments that make these organizations grow and succeed.” Links Evan Drellich at The Athletic last week posted a thorough overview of the pending MLB work stoppage , a piece that’s chock full of details. He also offered this assessment among the many insights in the article: But there’s another way to parse the situation. The owners might also view an offseason lockout — and maybe a relatively small number of missed games — as a low-risk opportunity to go for what they really want. If that doesn’t work, they move on, and try to leverage the fact they backed off a cap. Hall of Fame baseball writer Ross Newhan, who among other stops wrote for the Los Angeles Times for 37 years, died last week at age 89. item.title: Barca equal to PSG, Real Madrid, insists Gordon
item.description: Barcelona winger Anthony Gordon said his team were not below the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid (Josep LAGO) Barcelona winger Anthony Gordon insisted Monday his team are not below the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, despite recent defeats by both sides. Hansi Flick's side were unbeaten until facing European champions PSG on October 20, but lost 4-2 in Paris before a 2-1 Clasico defeat at home on October 25 by Madrid. Spanish title holders Barcelona last won the Champions League in 2015 and questions remain about their ability on the biggest occasions. "I don't think they're above (us). We have to take responsibility for both losses because they're the two biggest games we played so far this season and we lost, but I don't think they're above us," Gordon told reporters. "I think we're a fantastic team and on any given day we can beat anybody. In these two games, the PSG game has a bit of context... on the weekend in their league they rested their whole team. "We didn't have this privilege, so we were really tired in the game. This is normal, fine, we have to take responsibility, but I think they had a massive advantage with this." Gordon said his team deserved to win the Clasico, which Real Madrid claimed with a late goal from Kylian Mbappe as Barca's defence crumbled. "Madrid is the one game, the most important game we want to win. For me we should have," continued Gordon. "For me were there much better team in the game, we had all the ball, all the possession, the better chances, but we were a slight bit off our best game. It cost us in the end, we conceded two very bad goals. "Against this kind of opposition and this level of player it can really hurt you in these games. We'll learn for next time and I'm really excited to play these type of teams again to show what we can do." Barca host Premier League side Aston Villa on Tuesday as they aim to get back on track in the Champions League, before visiting Atletico Madrid on Sunday in La Liga. "I'm always motivated the same... the fact they're English doesn't make it more motivating for me," said Gordon ahead of Villa's visit to Camp Nou. "They're a very good team... they have a great coach (Unai Emery), one of the best in the world... it's going to be a very difficult game." Villa hold a 100 percent record so far in the Champions League, defeating Viking, Fenerbahce and Club Brugge. Barcelona signed Gordon from Newcastle in the summer for a fee which could rise to 80 million euros ($89m). The 25-year-old has three goals and five assists in 13 appearances for Barcelona across all competitions, but said his best is yet to come. "It's a big change, a new team, it's been a massive change for me and my family," added Gordon. "I've started well but like I've said numerous times, I can do more. It will take some time to grow, feel settled, and then when this happens I think you'll see the very best of me, which you definitely haven't seen so far." rbs/lp

item.title: Brysen Wright nears decision. Who are five-star receiver's finalists?
item.description: Decision time is near for Brysen Wright. The five-star Mandarin wide receiver, ranked before the season by USA TODAY as the No. 1 high school football prospect in the United States for the 2028 recruiting class, is scheduled to announce his college decision on Thursday, Nov. 5 from a finalist trio of Florida, Miami and Texas. The news was first announced by Rivals, and subsequently reposted to Wright's personal Instagram account . Here's what fans need to know. Brysen Wright: Florida, Miami or Texas? Wright has been in the recruiting spotlight for a long, long time. He was already projected as one of Jacksonville's premier prospects before his first snap at Mandarin, and became a viral online sensation through his gravity-defying catches during off-season work in flag football. A tall and physically dominant receiver, noted for his catching ability in traffic and his dizzying escapes from tacklers in the open field, he also earned the NFL Flag Player of the Year for 2025 and was honored during an NFL ceremony in February held during the week of the Super Bowl. Through two full seasons and a still-active third, Wright has recorded 121 catches for 2,592 yards and 29 touchdowns as a receiver in 33 games. Most of those receptions have come from the arm of fellow Mandarin junior Knox Annis, who committed to Miami in April. In addition, Wright has developed as an impact kick and punt returner as well as a quality safety. As a sophomore, Wright made 55 tackles with five interceptions and five pass breakups, plus two punt returns. He also competed in basketball during his first two seasons at Mandarin. Playing both sides of the football, he has helped the Mustangs to a 9-1 regular season record and an expected No. 1 seed in the Florida High School Athletic Association Region 1-5A playoffs beginning on Nov. 13. All three of Wright's finalist schools have recent track records of signing players from Mandarin. Florida's roster includes former quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. and safety Drake Stubbs; Miami signed offensive lineman Deryc Plazz (subsequently transferred to Auburn) and cornerback Brody Jennings; and Texas signed wide receiver Jaime Ffrench Jr., who has since transferred to Michigan. item.description: FOXBOROUGH — The season-high crowd of 54,112 that filled Gillette Stadium on Sunday night got a reminder of why Lionel Messi is considered the GOAT of professional soccer. The Argentine superstar broke a 1-1 tie with his league-leading 26th goal in the 83rd minute to lift defending MLS champion Inter Miami CF to a 2-1 victory over the New England Revolution. The Revolution had their four-game winning streak snapped and fell to 18-11-4 overall and 11-4-2 at Gillette Stadium. Inter Miami improved to 16-6-11 and moved past the Revolution into second place in the Eastern Conference. The Revolution can regain the No. 2 seed in the upcoming MLS playoffs with a win next Saturday at Orlando City combined with an Inter Miami loss against Charlotte. “From a standings perspective, it was not our intention tonight to chase the second position,” said first-year Revolution head coach Marco Mitrovic. “Our intention was that we had a champion of the league in front of us and we wanted to see who we are and how we can compete against the best teams in the league. I actually think it was a very good game.” Messi made a masterful move to secure the game-winner. He forced a turnover, dribbled past three Revolution defenders and into the penalty area, then delivered a surgical strike that sailed past goalkeeper Matt Turner and inside the far post. “When you play against Messi, who is arguably the best player in the history of the game, they have those inspirational moments and he has a high level of execution,” Mitrovic said. “Players at the highest level have that inside them. “They can convert those small situations in their favor and we had good control of Messi up until then. One thing with players like Messi, they have that inspirational moment that can change a game.” Moments after Messi put Inter Miami ahead, the Revolution appeared to tie the game at 2-2 on an own goal by defender Ian Fray. Referee Sergil Boika reviewed the play and disallowed the goal after determining that Revolution player Luca Lombardo was offside. The Revolution played their third game in nine days near the end of a long campaign. Mitrovic made two changes to the starting XI that secured a 3-2 victory over the New York Red Bulls on Wednesday night at Gillette Stadium. Mitrovic replaced Jackson Yueill with defensive midfielder Matt Polster, who was making his 245th career MLS start, while Peyton Miller was inserted on the right wing in place of Langoni, who came on as a late substitute. item.description: Josh Jacobs is facing an expanded NFL investigation after new allegations surfaced involving three additional women. The Green Bay Packers running back was initially accused of throwing his then-girlfriend to the ground during a physical confrontation in his garage in May 2026. However, a Hobart-Lawrence Police Department report obtained by NBC reportedly revealed that three other women had also accused Jacobs of physical abuse. The Packers running back missed six games this season while on the exempt list, but he is currently cleared to remain active. The NFL has since confirmed that investigators will also review the latest allegations as part of the ongoing case, according to Tom Pelissero’s post on X (formerly Twitter). From the NFL: “We will review these allegations as part of the investigation which has remained open.” https://t.co/jHsAE4oPu3 — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) October 31, 2026 “We will review these allegations as part of the investigation which has remained open,” the league commented . The newly obtained police documents detail three separate accusations involving Jacobs from 2021 and 2022, dating back to his time with the Las Vegas Raiders. These accounts describe alleged incidents involving different women and add to the investigation surrounding a May 23, 2026, incident that led to Jacobs’ arrest three days later. New details emerge on Josh Jacobs allegations Oct 29, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs (8) reacts after rushing for a touchdown against Carolina Panthers linebacker Bobby Okereke (58) in the second half at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Jacobs initially faced five charges following his arrest , including a felony count of strangulation. The case later concluded with a plea agreement covering two misdemeanors, battery and criminal damage to property. In a statement released Saturday, Jacobs’ attorneys described the additional allegations as outdated, unsupported and never previously reported. They also said the Brown County District Attorney’s Office worked closely with police on an extensive investigation before deciding that only two misdemeanor charges were appropriate. Oct 25, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs (8) celebrates a touchdown during the third quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images The latest accusations have not led to any additional criminal charges against Jacobs. item.description: Image Credit: TMZ/ Facebook. Freddie James, the longtime Dallas Carter High School football coach, has died at 89. His family confirmed that he died Thursday morning, October 29, according to a Dallas Morning News report republished by Texas Metro News . Julius Tennon played James in the 2004 film Friday Night Lights . Charles S. Dutton later portrayed him in the 2015 drama Carter High . South Oak Cliff coach Jason Todd credited James with setting a standard for success that helped shape his own coaching ambitions. "He was an icon," Todd told the newspaper. On October 29, Dallas ISD trustees approved a waiver allowing Carter's athletic complex to be named in James' honor. James Built Carter Into a Texas Football Power Born Freddie Lee James on July 25, 1937, in Atlanta, Texas, he earned a scholarship to Prairie View A&M University. He played running back and defensive back on its 1958 Black college national championship team. His coaching career began in 1964 at Spigner High School in Calvert, Texas. He later joined Dallas ISD and worked as an assistant at Carter before taking charge of its football program in 1982. The Dallas Morning News credited James with a 139-27-5 record across 14 seasons leading Carter. Eight of his players reached the NFL, including New York Giants All-Pro linebacker Jessie Armstead and two-time San Francisco 49ers Super Bowl champion Chet Brooks. James received eight Dallas ISD Coach of the Year awards. He also joined the inaugural Texas Black Sports Hall of Fame class in 1996 and the Dallas ISD Athletic Hall of Fame's first class in 2018. item.title: Paul Finebaum goes off after latest Oklahoma loss: ‘Brent Venables is dead’
item.description: Credit: ESPN Paul Finebaum, a recent guest on the Awful Announcing Podcast , has never been shy with his opinions. True to form, he’s been letting the hot takes fly this college football season, and on Sunday, Finebaum let Oklahoma Sooners head football coach Brent Venables have it. Finebaum and Matt Barrie recapped Saturday’s college football action on The Matt Barrie Show , and Barrie asked Finebaum for his thoughts on the South Carolina Gamecocks after their 42-25 win over the Sooners. “I was really interested in that game yesterday because I can’t get away from Oklahoma and how they started the season inside the top 10—and how Brent Venables was just given an extension by their new athletic director who came over from Illinois,” Finebaum said. “I have rarely seen a guy limping more than Venables right now.” “Conversely, four weeks ago, [South Carolina head coach] Shane Beamer was dead,” Finebaum continued. “Nobody’s dead in this sport! It is a little bit like Halloween. I mean, Lincoln Riley, you name the coach, and they have come back from the dead. Although, I am going to tell you right now: Brent Venables is dead. He is not getting back. He is out of ammunition. This has been an abject disaster for him, and unfortunately for Oklahoma fans, they are stuck with him.” By losing to South Carolina, Oklahoma fell to 4-4 overall and 2-3 in conference play on the year. Venables opened his postgame press conference like a man who is well aware of the pressure he’s up against. “I’m not going to say a whole lot other than just the obvious,” Venables said. “I’m not gonna sit here and try to explain or excuse or anything else. Got our a** whooped tonight in every way and really disappointed.” It won’t get any easier for the Sooners, either. This time it came against the previously AFC West leading Kansas City Chiefs. With 15-unanswered points in the fourth quarter and a heck of a goal to go stand to send the Broncos into first place in the division and the second seeded spot in the AFC . item.title: Cooper Flagg's Dirk Nowitzki wish could be granted by Mavericks after electric second-season start
item.description: Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images The Dallas Mavericks’ Cooper Flagg has become one of the most exciting names in basketball since the start of the new NBA season. The 2025 Rookie of the Year has been viewed as a huge talent for well over a year now, but he has taken his game to an even higher level this campaign. Flagg owes a lot to the Mavs for his development since he joined them, so much so that he’s ready to commit his entire career to the franchise. Now, after his brilliant start to the new season, he stands a great chance of getting his wish. Cooper Flagg’s dream of following Dirk Nowitzki could come true A 19-year-old basketball player who is considered an elite talent would usually have ambitions to play for the best team in the NBA at all times. However, for Flagg, the Dallas Mavericks is home already, and if it were up to him, he’d stay there for the rest of his professional career. The teenager pointed to Dirk Nowitzki and how he is regarded as a legend in Dallas for spending the entirety of his 21-year career there. Flagg would love to follow in the same footsteps, but he was mature enough to understand that it’s not in his hands and the business of basketball could easily take him to another franchise. When asked if he would want to stay forever in Dallas, he said on the Almost Athletes with Dude Perfect show in June: “100 per cent! “I think I would like nothing more than that to be able to… you look at someone like Dirk, obviously, his legacy, there’s nothing that touches that, to be that loved by a city, to have that much love and support from one place. I don’t think you could dream for anything else but that. “That’s the ultimate goal, but like we were just talking about, it’s a business at the end of the day, and it’s not going to be my decision, I don’t think.” It’s not going to be Flagg’s decision alone, but after a great rookie year and an electric start to his second season, the Mavericks would be silly to even consider letting him go. Kyrie Irving is being linked with other teams, but for the Dallas front office, the aim is to build a long-term competitive future around Flagg under head coach Dusty May. For that reason, unless something extremely drastic happens, we think Flagg’s wish to stay with the Dallas Mavericks for his entire career has a high chance of being granted. item.title: The Lions called a tricky CFL play to set up a touchdown
item.description: The Detroit Lions’ offense has the unenviable task of trying to score points on the mighty Minnesota Vikings defense in their Week 8 matchup. Minnesota’s defense might not be historic , but it is very, very good with Brian Flores calling the shots in a blitz-heavy scheme. Minnesota is the only undefeated team in the league entering the week at 6-0, but the offense is so uninspiring that there are currently 11 teams ahead of them in FanDuel’s NFL championship odds . The Lions’ offense has been really good even after losing former OC Ben Johnson a couple seasons ago to the Chicago Bears. Detroit is still coming up with some really interesting passing concepts to complement Jamir Gibbs in the running game, and they used one of them to convert a long 3rd-and-8 in the third quarter against Minnesota. Detroit pulled a play straight out of the CFL by lining up star receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown 15-yards behind the line of scrimmage, then letting him get a running start to catch a screen pass and convert the first down. The Lions would score a touchdown on the next play, and go on to beat the Vikings, 19-15, to give Minnesota its first loss of the year. Watch the critical third down conversion here: An interesting play by the Lions for the first down. 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/ymTgoRrpJT — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) November 1, 2026 You see this type of play often in the CFL, where it’s legal for eligible receivers off the line to be in continuous motion in any direction at the snap of the ball. The NFL restricts motion to a single player moving horizontally or backward, but this play is legal because St. Brown doesn’t actually move until the snap. The Lions put Goff in a shotgun so he could build up speed and hit the flat as soon as he was ready to throw. As long St. Brown reports as eligible and the Lions have the required amount of players on the line of scrimmage, the play is legal. Detroit had a TE in the los on the left side of the formation to fulfill the line requirement Jahmyr Gibbs busted a 30-yard touchdown run on the next play to give Detroit the lead. The Lions improved to 5-2 with the win, but the focus will be on the status of injured linebacker Jack Campbell who was carted off after lying motionless on the field . This was a cool play for the Lions in a great win. Let’s just hope Campbell is okay.
